paper_metadata.title: Effect of heat treatment and thermomechanical processing on microstructure and tensile property of Ti-44Al-8Nb-0.2W-0.2B-0.5Y alloy

evidence.quote: High Nb-TiAl (Ti-44Al-8Nb-0.2W-0.2B-0.5Y, at.%) ingot was fabricated by vacuum arc remelting (VAR).
The solidification path of this high Nb-TiAl alloy is: L→L+β→β→α+β→α→α+β+γ→α2+β+γ.
The high Nb-TiAl alloy ingot with the nominal chemical composition of Ti-44Al-8Nb-0.2W-0.2B-0.5Y (at.%) was fabricated by vacuum arc remelting (V AR).

evidence.quote: the as-cast high Nb-TiAl alloy ingot was subjected to hot-isostatic pressing at 1,300 °C and 120 MPa for 3 h under argon atmosphere with the following furnace cooling, and a homogenizing annealing process was performed at 1,250 °C for 6 h after HIP.

evidence.section: 2.2 Effect of heat treatment on microstructure
evidence.quote: the alloy samples after HIP and annealing were heated at temperatures of 1,400 °C, 1,340 °C and 1,250 °C for 30 min, respectively, followed by water quenching or furnace cooling.

evidence.section: 2.2 Effect of heat treatment on microstructure

evidence.section: 2.2 Effect of heat treatment on microstructure

Compared with tensile property of the high Nb-TiAl alloy before forging, the ultimate tensile strength of forged high Nb-TiAl alloy in furnace cooled condition is increased from 538 MPa to 820 MPa, and the elongation at room temperature increases from 0.3% to 0.9%.
